findings.evidence: `src/main.rs` accepts `--quiet` before the file and passes it to
findings.location: design.md#Decision: The progress reporter takes a `quiet` switch
findings.recommendation: State in the spec where `--quiet` may appear and add a scenario for the other position (`ledger import data.csv --quiet`): either accept it, or name the outcome (today `src/main.rs:6-10` falls to the usage error, exit code 2, and nothing is imported). A nightly script that appends the flag would otherwise stop importing, which is worse than the noise the Why complains about.
findings.title: Flag position is unspecified; the design rejects `--quiet` after the file

findings.evidence: - [ ] 1.1 `--quiet` read by `src/main.rs`, added to `FLAGS` in `src/cli/import.rs` and passed to `Progress::new(quiet)`
findings.recommendation: `src/main.rs:8` prints `usage: ledger import <file>`; no task or decision changes it, so the CLI's own help would keep hiding the new flag while `docs/cli.md` documents it. Add the update of the usage line to task 1.1.
findings.title: The usage line is not updated to mention `--quiet`

findings.recommendation: The change alters the command line's user-visible output and the output of scheduled jobs (the Why: "Nightly scripts run `ledger import`"). Either tick `user-interface` / `operations`, or keep them unticked with the reason on their line (`- [ ] <domain> — <reason>`), so that no expert's domain is left to nobody silently.
